findings.current: You just startled me. You were sleeping soundly, then suddenly woke up. The first thing you saw when you opened your eyes was my face.
findings.defect: The draft makes Jin the sleeper who wakes and sees Sudal. Sudal is explaining why his father punched him.
findings.rationale: The omitted subject of the honorific verbs is Sudal’s father, mentioned immediately before this explanation.
findings.replacement: My father was just startled. He’d been sleeping soundly, then suddenly woke up and saw my face the moment he opened his eyes.
findings.source: 단지 너무 놀라셨을 뿐이에요. 잘 주무시다가 불현듯 잠에서 깨어나셨는데, 눈을 뜨자마자 제 얼굴을 보셨거든요.

findings.current: “Ah, do I really have to shout this loudly? The Captain’s already exhausted. What if he gets qi deviation? Why would you do that to him?”
findings.defect: Hwaran is objecting to Sudal’s shouting, not asking whether she herself must shout.
findings.rationale: 저러는 거지 refers to the pirate leader’s conduct; Hwaran is muttering about the noise he makes.
findings.replacement: “Ah, does he have to shout so loudly? The Captain’s already exhausted. What if all that noise gives him qi deviation? What’s he thinking?”
findings.source: 아, 꼭 이 정도로 시끄럽게 소리 질러야 하나? 가뜩이나 조장님 힘드신데. 주화입마라도 걸리면 어쩌려고 저러는 거지?

findings.current: When I finished thinking and let out a quiet laugh, Namho’s eyes widened. Then he, too, gave a bitter smile.
findings.defect: The narration omits that Jin speaks the preceding line, leaving Namho’s reaction attributed only to a laugh.
findings.rationale: 내뱉은 한 마디 explicitly identifies Jin’s spoken remark as what prompts Namho’s reaction.
findings.replacement: I finished thinking, gave a quiet laugh, and said it aloud. Namho’s eyes widened at my words. Then he, too, gave a bitter smile.
findings.source:
“잘들 노네요.”

생각을 끝마친 내가 피식 웃으며 내뱉은 한 마디에, 남호의 눈이 크게 뜨였다. 그리고 이내 그 역시 쓴웃음을 머금었다.

findings.current: The eyes of Sudal—sea otter, whatever-the-hell otter—suddenly flashed.
findings.defect: The final iteration of the running name joke, Heimdall, is replaced with an invented otter phrase; the unfocused state of his eyes is also lost.
findings.rationale: The source repeats all three names in sequence and contrasts his previously unfocused eyes with their sudden sharpness.
findings.replacement: Sudal, Sea Otter, Heimdall—whatever his name was—his unfocused eyes suddenly flashed.
findings.source: 초점이 흐릿하던 해달, 수달, 헤임달의 눈동자가 번뜩인다.

findings.current: What did I have to worry about, military vessels or not?
findings.defect: The neutral concession flattens Jin’s profane dismissal of the military vessels.
findings.rationale: 나발이고 brusquely rejects the concern rather than weighing whether the vessels are military.
findings.replacement: Military vessels, my ass. What was there to worry about?

findings.defect: The medical concern loses the blood component of 기혈.
findings.rationale: 기혈 names both qi and blood in the bodily condition Jin asks about.
findings.replacement: Are your qi and blood all tangled up?

findings.current: The fireworks kept exploding as the military vessels turned sideways.
findings.defect: Turning simply ‘sideways’ loses the angled maneuver that presents the vessels’ sides.
findings.rationale: 비스듬히 specifies an angled turn; 옆면 sets up the cannon openings revealed immediately afterward.
findings.replacement: Fireworks burst one after another as the military vessels angled around to present their broadsides.
findings.source: 연달아 터지는 폭죽과 함께 비스듬히 옆면으로 회전하는 군선들.

findings.current: Over a hundred cannon barrels belched fire at once.
findings.defect: ‘Over a hundred’ changes an approximate count into a lower bound.
findings.rationale: 백여 개 means approximately a hundred, not necessarily more than a hundred.
findings.replacement: About a hundred cannon barrels belched fire at once.
findings.source: 백여 개의 포신(砲身)이 동시에 화염을 내뿜었다.

summary: Several subject and action errors affect the dialogue, alongside losses in the name joke, medical wording, and final cannon count.
